metadata.name: SpectraCQ
metadata.description: Competency-question benchmark for the SPECTRA 3GPP-RAN process knowledge graph; each CQ pairs a natural-language question with executable Cypher and a deterministic gold answer set obtained by re-executing the Cypher against the live graph (no LLM in the gold path).
metadata.company_names: verbatim public 3GPP identifiers (single-blind venue; no anonymization)
metadata.held_policy: CQs with empty or uniformly zero/false gold against the live graph (entity-layer constructs not materialized in the operational graph, or genuinely-empty answer sets) are held out of the scored set to avoid degenerate set-scoring; they ship under held/ with Cypher + status.

primary_values_preview:
RAN1 agreed that “After initial cell selection, the UE is expected to find a single SCS per frequency layer” in RAN1#90 meeting and informed RAN2 in LS (R2-1815956). 
According to RAN1 agreements, the single SCS per frequency restriction is applicable for both CONNECTED and IDLE/INACTIVE state.  

For CONNECTED state, RAN2 reflected the single SCS per frequency layer restriction in MO configuration and captured it in section 5.5.2.1 in RRC. 
-	to ensure that all measurement objects configured in this specification and in TS 36.331 [10] with the same ssbFrequency have the same ssbSubcarrierSpacing;
But there is no clarification of this restriction for IDLE/INACTIVE state. 
For IDLE/INACTIVE state, network can provide the frequency and SCS information in SIB4, SIB11, or in RRCRelease with measIdleConfig message. 
If there is no clarification on the single SCS per frequency layer restriction in IDLE/INACTIVE state, it’s not clear whether the restriction is applicable across all the IDLE/INACTIVE configuration across different kind of configurations.

cqs.question_en: Return the summary of change of CR R2-2508534 (change overview).

primary_values_preview:
Add the single SCS per frequency layer restriction in general in Clause 9.2.4 Measurements, and it’s applicable for RRC_IDLE state, RRC_INACTIVE state and RRC_CONNECTED state.  

Impact Analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: 
NR SA, NR-DC, NE-DC, EN-DC
 
Impacted functionality: 
Inter-frequency cell re-selection
 
Inter-operability: 
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, the UE may consider the network configuration is incorrect.

cqs.question_en: Return the consequences if CR R2-2508534 is not approved (adoption urgency).

primary_values_preview: There may be the misunderstanding that multiple SCSs per frequency is supported in IDLE/INACTIVE state, which will increase the UE complexity.

primary_values_preview: In conclusion of the study, the following enhancements for XR services are recommended: -	For XR Awareness: -	Provisioning by CN of semi-static information per QoS flow (e.g. PDU set QoS parameters), dynamic information per PDU set (PDU Set information and Identification) and End of Data Burst indication (as per TR 23.700-60 [9]); -	Identifying by UE of PDU Sets, Data bursts and PSI; -	Provisioning by UE of XR traffic assistance information e.g. periodicity, UL traffic arrival information (FFS). -	For Power Saving: -	DRX support of XR frame rates corresponding to non-integer periodicities (through at least semi-static mechanisms e.g. RRC signalling). -	For Capacity Enhancements: -	Multiple CG PUSCH transmission occasions in a period of a single CG PUSCH configuration; -	Dynamic indication

primary_values_preview:
When two location reporting events should be setup in the Initial Context Setup procedure, only one event can be signalled  in a single Location Reporting procedure. It is beneficial to allow signaling two location reporting events in one message.

When AMF wants to stop reporting UE presence in the mulitple area of interest, it has to sent multipe Location Reporting Control Messages. This is inefficient and the reporting may not be able to be stopped in time.

primary_values_preview: In this TR, failure scenario in the existing gNB-CU-CP architecture from various perspectives were studied. A failure affecting the entire (logical) gNB-CU-CP would impact all UEs served by the cells of the gNB-DUs connected to the gNB-CU-CP, resulting in those UEs being out of service for potentially long periods of time (dependent on type of failure and available resiliency measures). Current specification allows for some resiliency mechanisms via appropriate implementation (as described in TS 38.401[2]) which can address a number of the failure scenarios.
